newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN SET TO START BIDDING WAR.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN SET TO START BIDDING WAR.

text.p: Three-time motorcycle world champion Michael Doohan is ready to start a bidding war for his services next season after confirming he has put his retirement plans on hold.
The veteran Honda rider, who holds a massive lead in this season's riders' championship, said he would listen to offers from rival teams, the Melbourne Age newspaper said on Friday.
"The other guys (teams) are pretty desperate for some results. They might pull something big out," the 32-year-old Australian was quoted as saying.
"If someone wants to poach me they have to pay, it's the same in any sport -- I don't have to prove myself. I'm a racer and I like to win."
Doohan, who had hinted in the past he would retire at the end of the 1997 season, said he would make a decision about his future employment after the San Marino Grand Prix at Imola on July 6.
But Doohan did not rule out staying with Honda, the team he has helped lift to a position of total domination in recent seasons.
"Honda always put their money where their mouth is," said Doohan, who is reportedly paid about A$6 million (US4.5 million) a season by the Japanese manufacturer.
Doohan leads the riders' championship by 43 points from teammate Alex Criville of Spain after six rounds.
"When I was 23 you think 32 is old and I thought when I made it that far it would be enough," Doohan said.
"But now I'm 32 I feel I haven't done enough racing yet, at this stage I feel like I'll keep going another year at least."

Despite his greying hair and a battered right leg, which almost needed amputating after a high-speed crash at Assen in 1992, Doohan shows no sign of losing his appetite for Grand Prix wins. His tally stands at 39.
"At the moment I have no idea what I would do when I stop racing so I guees that means I'm not ready to stop racing.
"I'm still enjoying the racing and I'm still winning GPs. As soon as I stop enjoying it I'll be out of here," he said.
